title: DrivAerML-to-SHIFT-SUV validation-only adaptation pilot
scientific_question: Does a DrivAerML-trained initialization reduce the number of SHIFT-SUV target simulations needed, and is any reduction larger for MeshTransformer than for GeoTransolver?

scope.claim_limit: conditional evidence only; not an untouched-family or physics-specific-transfer claim
scope.test_policy: No test case may be read, trained on, or evaluated during this pilot.

activation_gate.requirement: The checkpoint-era MeshTransformer must complete finite forward/loss evaluations on its DrivAerML source canary before any target result is interpretable.
activation_gate.if_failed: Do not launch or interpret the validation pilot; repair provenance instead.
activation_gate.evidence: HSG job 5701700 completed finite source, estate, and fastback lanes under checkpoint-era model and gauge semantics.

protocol_amendments.information_used: Compatibility-canary finiteness and step time on training-origin cases only; no registered validation case or pilot outcome was inspected.
protocol_amendments.reason: Eager execution preserved finite adaptation while avoiding shape-specialized compilation overhead; 70 equal target exposures fit every 128-case arm inside the cluster's four-hour job limit.

protocol_amendments.information_used: A registered learning-rate arm triggered the prospective non-finite-loss guard; no cross-arm validation ranking or label-efficiency contrast was inspected.

changes.divergent_candidate_handling: A learning-rate arm that terminates at the non-finite guard retains every fully completed registered checkpoint as an eligible early-stopping candidate. Later unavailable checkpoints have infinite selection error. The same rule applies to every architecture and initialization.

protocol_amendments.reason: The frozen rule selects a learning-rate and stored-epoch pair. A later divergence does not invalidate an earlier finite stored epoch, but it cannot create missing later candidates or be treated as ordinary missing data.

protocol_amendments.information_used: A code-path audit showed that the training loop's random 10,000-cell validation subsample advances after the training iterator and therefore differs by epoch and label budget. Stored validation values or cross-arm rankings were not inspected.

changes.formal_validation_evaluation: Re-evaluate every eligible registered checkpoint on two dedicated validation-only passes with fixed seeds 20260730 and 20260731. Do not iterate the training loader. Average the two point-subsample measurements within each validation case before checkpoint selection and all derived comparisons.
changes.training_loop_validation_metrics: Retain for run-integrity diagnostics only; do not use them for formal selection or scientific ratios.
changes.fixed_evaluation_non_finite_rule: A checkpoint that is non-finite on either fixed evaluation pass has infinite selection error. Other stored checkpoints from the same learning-rate arm remain eligible.

protocol_amendments.reason: A common fixed point sample makes the 99 cases genuinely paired across architecture, initialization, learning rate, epoch, and label budget while retaining the registered 10,000-cell model resolution.

protocol_amendments.information_used: Only the frozen training horizon and the logical distinction between target-label efficiency and faster optimization were used. No online or fixed-validation metric, checkpoint ranking, or cross-arm outcome was inspected.

changes.optimization_horizon_gate: If either selected checkpoint in a half-label comparison is the final registered epoch, interpret that comparison only as fixed-exposure learning-speed evidence. It cannot establish that fewer target simulations suffice until a prospectively extended horizon shows that the ordering survives.

protocol_amendments.reason: A scratch model that is still improving could catch up without receiving another target simulation. Equal target exposures therefore control optimization time but do not by themselves prove asymptotic label efficiency.

protocol_amendments.information_used: Only the frozen three-point learning-rate grid and the logical distinction between within-grid selection and a bracketed optimum were used. No online or fixed-validation metric, checkpoint ranking, or cross-arm outcome was inspected.

changes.optimization_grid_flag: A half-label comparison is optimizer-bracketed only when both selected learning rates are the interior grid value. A boundary selection remains valid within-grid pilot evidence, but confirmation must add a stable flanking or intermediate rate before supporting an optimized target-label-efficiency claim.

protocol_amendments.reason: Symmetric tuning does not prove a fair optimum if either selected model is censored by the edge of the registered search grid.

rival_hypotheses.reusable_source_knowledge: Pretraining lowers validation error at fixed target-label budget and can match the scratch model with half as many target cases.
rival_hypotheses.generic_adaptation: MeshTransformer and GeoTransolver receive similar relative benefit; reuse is real but boundary-aware structure has no incremental support.
rival_hypotheses.geometry_conditional_reuse: The source benefit changes materially or reverses between estate and fastback.
rival_hypotheses.specialist_regression: Pretraining is neutral or harmful after symmetric validation selection.

data.nesting_rule: For each family, train_64 is a strict subset of train_128 and both are disjoint from validation.

selection_rule.primary_metric: mean per-case pressure relative L2 on all 99 validation cases, after averaging fixed point-subsample seeds 20260730 and 20260731 within case
selection_rule.secondary_metric: mean per-case wall-shear-stress vector relative L2 under the same fixed evaluation
selection_rule.procedure: Within each architecture, initialization, family, and label budget, choose the learning-rate and stored-epoch pair with the lowest primary metric.
selection_rule.tie_breaker: If primary metrics are exactly equal, choose the earlier completed epoch, then the smaller learning rate.
selection_rule.symmetry: Apply the identical grid and selection rule to scratch and pretrained arms.
selection_rule.non_finite_rule: A guard-terminated learning-rate arm contributes its fully completed registered checkpoints; all later checkpoints are assigned infinite selection error.
selection_rule.fixed_evaluation_non_finite_rule: A checkpoint that is non-finite on either fixed evaluation pass is ineligible; this does not remove other stored checkpoints from the arm.

fixed_validation_evaluation.loader_rule: Build the registered manifest dataset, set the validation loader epoch to zero, and iterate only the sequential validation sampler.
fixed_validation_evaluation.aggregation: Average each metric across the two fixed point-subsample seeds within case, then average across the 99 cases.
fixed_validation_evaluation.coverage: Every eligible registered checkpoint is evaluated; terminal arms have no candidates after their first guard.

prospective_decision_rules.field_safety: At the half-label comparison, pretrained wall-shear-stress error may not exceed scratch error by more than 10%.
prospective_decision_rules.strong_validation_signal: The paired case bootstrap 95% upper bound for H is below 1.0; this is descriptive because validation also selected hyperparameters.
prospective_decision_rules.optimization_horizon_gate: A half-label comparison supports target-label efficiency only when neither selected checkpoint is the final registered epoch. Otherwise it supports fixed-exposure learning speed only and requires a prospectively extended horizon.
prospective_decision_rules.optimization_grid_flag: A half-label comparison supports an optimized target-label-efficiency claim only when both selected learning rates are the interior grid value. A boundary selection may advance as within-grid pilot evidence, but its confirmation must refine the learning-rate bracket.
prospective_decision_rules.advance_to_confirmation: Advance an architecture only if material half-label success, field safety, and the optimization-horizon gate hold on both families.
prospective_decision_rules.do_not_open_test: The sealed tests remain unopened until confirmation seeds, hyperparameters, epoch, and final decision thresholds are frozen.

interpretation_limits: One source checkpoint and one target seed cannot establish a general transfer law.
A larger architecture interaction may reflect source-checkpoint quality as well as architecture.
Because SHIFT-SUV family identity has been inspected previously, this pilot cannot restore an untouched-family claim.
An unrelated-pretraining control would be required to isolate physics-specific transfer.
